bank.q: Which is true of Java inheritance?
options: A class can extend two classes
A class extends exactly one class
private members are directly usable in the child

bank.q: What does super(name) do in a subclass constructor?
bank.why: It must be the first line.

options: It makes the compiler check the method really overrides

bank.q: Parent p = new Child(); p.childOnly(); gives?
options: Compile error: Parent has no childOnly()

bank.q: Which method can a subclass override?
bank.why: Private, static and final cannot be overridden.

bank.q: Child c = (Child) new Parent(); at run time throws?
bank.why: The real object is a Parent.

bank.q: Explain polymorphism with a short example.
bank.model: A parent reference can hold any child object and the real object decides which overridden method runs: Animal a = new Dog(); a.sound() prints Woof.

bank.q: Can you override a private or static method? Explain.
bank.model: No. Private methods are invisible to the subclass; a same-signature static method hides the parent's (method hiding) rather than overriding it.

bank.q: State two differences between overloading and overriding.
bank.model: Overloading: same class, different parameters, compile-time. Overriding: subclass, same signature, run-time.

bank.title: Mini project: Zoo
bank.brief: Write Animal (name, sound()), Dog, Cat and Cow that override sound(), and a Zoo class holding an ArrayList<Animal> that prints every animal's sound in one loop. Add a Bird later without changing Zoo.
